findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate by datetime; it crashes on the first page
findings.body: The audit log endpoint uses OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime", but OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does `math.floor(value)` / `math.ceil(value)` directly on the attribute value, which is a Python datetime object. math.floor/datetime raises TypeError (an integer is required). get_item_key is invoked by build_cursor on every result set (via _build_next_values/_build_prev_values), so the very first request using ?optimized_pagination=true will 500. This paginator needs the same epoch-milliseconds conversion DateTimePaginator performs (strftime('%s.%f') * multiplier).

findings.title: value_from_cursor returns a raw integer that is compared against a datetime column
findings.body: Even ignoring the crash, OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor returns cursor.value unchanged (an integer), and build_queryset injects it into `WHERE <table>.datetime <= %s`. For a datetime-ordered queryset the cursor value must be converted back to a datetime (as DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor does with fromtimestamp(value/1000)); comparing a datetime column to an integer epoch value will either error at the database level or silently match nothing/everything depending on coercion, corrupting pagination results.

findings.title: Negative cursor offsets are passed into queryset slicing, which Django rejects
findings.body: The comment claims 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically', but Django QuerySets explicitly do not support negative indexing: queryset[-5:95] raises ValueError ('Negative indexing is not supported'). Cursor offsets come from the client-supplied cursor string (`value:offset:is_prev`), which Cursor.from_string parses with int() and no validation, so any user with the optimized_pagination flag can send a negative offset and get a 500. The 'advanced feature' is non-functional and only adds a new error path.

findings.title: BasePaginator silently clamps negative forward-cursor offsets instead of rejecting them
findings.body: The change to BasePaginator.get_result replaces `results = list(queryset[offset:stop])` with `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`. A negative offset on a forward cursor previously raised a clear error; it is now silently treated as 0, so a client repeating a malformed/rewound cursor gets the first page again, which can cause infinite loops in polling consumers that keep following next cursors. Additionally, for is_prev cursors the raw (possibly negative) offset is still used in slicing and in the `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check, making that boundary check inconsistent with the clamped slice in the non-prev path.

findings.title: organization_context.member may be None, causing AttributeError before the optimized branch
findings.body: `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` dereferences organization_context.member unconditionally for non-superusers. Requests authenticated without an organization membership context (e.g., certain token-based or org-auth-token flows that ControlSiloOrganizationEndpoint permits) have member=None, so this raises AttributeError and 500s the endpoint even though the user was never going to use the optimized path. Guard with `organization_context.member is not None and ...` or getattr.

findings.title: No tests cover OptimizedCursorPaginator or the optimized audit log path
findings.body: The PR adds ~100 lines of new pagination logic plus a new endpoint branch gated by query param and permissions, but no tests. Basic coverage (first page, next/prev cursor round trip, negative offset handling, non-privileged user requesting optimized_pagination, datetime ordering) would have immediately caught the math.floor(datetime) crash and the negative-slicing ValueError.
